program.name: astryx
program.description: Design system CLI — components, themes, and tooling

options.description: output the version number
Simplified Chinese for component reads and for docs topics that have a translation (English otherwise)
Token-efficient dense text for component <Name> and docs <topic> reads
Language or format for component and docs reads: en (default), zh (as --zh), or dense (as --dense)

Detail level for component, hook, and docs tree reads (e.g. docs cli/commands/build), and for theme build reports. Lists default to brief; theme build prints one line per built theme unless full, which adds the install example and font recipe
Output as typed JSON. Success envelope: { apiVersion, type, package?, data, meta? }. Error envelope: { apiVersion, error, code, suggestions? }.

program.afterHelp:
Output format
Text mirrors --json (the machine-readable surface); it is built from these blocks:

block: Record
shape: aligned "key: value" lines = one item; records separated by a blank line

block: Section
shape: a header line (no "key:"), optional one-line subtitle, then its records/list

block: List
shape: "- value" lines for a simple sequence of values

block: Text
shape: free-form prose / notes

block: Code
shape: a verbatim block (source, skeleton, or doc), emitted exactly

Grep a field across records, e.g.   search button | grep "^command:". Errors/warnings go to stderr; use --json for structured parsing.

Global mode: in a project, the project's own CLI answers (this copy hands the run to it); a copy installed for the computer checks for updates once a day and keeps an agent skill in your home folder. See  docs global.

commands.name: init
commands.description: Initialize the design system in your project

options.description: Comma-separated features: agents (agent docs), theme (writes theme.template.ts), template (prints the page-building commands; writes no file). An unknown feature exits 1 with ERR_UNKNOWN_FEATURE. Refused with --all or --remove-agents
Install all features (agents, theme, template); refused with --features. Prints their guidance instead of the getting-started steps

Remove the managed block from AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .cursorrules, .hermes.md and HERMES.md, at the project root (where init writes them) and in this folder (deleting AGENTS.md or .claude/CLAUDE.md when only init's heading is left, and GEMINI.md when nothing is left) and do nothing else. Below the project root, a project-root agent file whose block resolves outside the project is left as it is, with a note. --features, --all, --agent and --agent-docs-path are refused; a file written with --agent-docs-path keeps its block

Write or refresh the computer-level agent text instead of setting up the folder: one skill file, ~/.agents/skills/astryx/SKILL.md, which most coding agents read, linked into the skill folders of agents that read only their own (~/.claude/skills always; Kiro, Windsurf, Letta, Xcode's coding assistant, and ~/.config/agents/skills when that folder exists): a folder symlink with a relative target, a junction on Windows, or a copy where neither can be made. Continue, whose scanner skips links, gets a managed copy, refreshed with the file. It tells agents anywhere on the computer that Astryx is there, when it is relevant, and to start with `astryx search`. Records the links it made in astryx/settings.json in the per-user configuration folder, so removal removes exactly those; the CLI installed for the computer refreshes the file in the background after each upgrade. Works in any folder. A file without the Astryx markers, one edited since Astryx wrote it, or a symlink, is kept as it is, and so is anything at a link target that Astryx did not create. Warns, and still writes, when no `astryx` command on the computer runs the Astryx CLI. With --remove-agents it removes the file, the links, and the copy instead and records that the text is turned off. --features, --all, --agent and --agent-docs-path are refused

Target AI tool for agent docs: claude (CLAUDE.md or .claude/CLAUDE.md, else creates .claude/CLAUDE.md), cursor (.cursorrules if present, else AGENTS.md), codex and muse (AGENTS.md), hermes (.hermes.md or HERMES.md if present, else AGENTS.md), all (every existing agent doc except GEMINI.md, which keeps its one-line import of AGENTS.md, else AGENTS.md and .claude/CLAUDE.md). With claude and all, when CLAUDE.md gets the block, .claude/CLAUDE.md gets none and a block already there is removed, unless the project ignores CLAUDE.md: then a .claude/CLAUDE.md the project commits gets a copy too, with claude and all alike. An unknown tool exits 1 with ERR_UNKNOWN_AGENT. Used only when agent docs are installed (the default, --all, or --features agents); --agent-docs-path takes precedence.

Explicit file path(s) for agent docs, inside the project; takes precedence over --agent. If any path is outside the project, no agent docs are written and the command exits 1. A path in the home folder itself, or in a settings folder in it outside a project (such as ~/.claude or ~/.claude/hooks), is refused with a note (exit 0), and nothing is written. Used only when agent docs are installed

commands.afterHelp:
Exit codes:
  0  success, including agent docs left unwritten in five soft cases, each reported as docsError with one note: running in the home folder, or in a settings folder in it outside a project; a GEMINI.md that resolves outside the project; when init runs below the project root, a project-root agent file that resolves outside the project; the project's Claude Code file (root CLAUDE.md, or .claude/CLAUDE.md when there is no root one) when it resolves outside the project and is a block-less import of an existing AGENTS.md, which 0.7.1 left alone; and a .claude/CLAUDE.md that resolves outside the project and that 0.7.1 did not write: beside a CLAUDE.md the project ignores, the one --agent claude adds or a block-less import of an existing AGENTS.md; with --agent claude beside a CLAUDE.md, one whose block it would remove
  1  an unknown --agent (ERR_UNKNOWN_AGENT) or feature, an --agent-docs-path outside the project, --remove-agents combined with install options, --user combined with --features, --all, --agent or --agent-docs-path, or --all with --features (ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT); or, when init runs at the project root, an agent file 0.7.1 also wrote there that resolves outside the project (ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL, docsError path-safety, nothing written)

Examples:
  # Default setup
   init
  # All features, no prompts
   init --all
  # Machine-readable receipt
   init --json
  # Agent text for the whole computer
   init --user
  # Remove the computer-level agent text and turn it off
   init --user --remove-agents

More:  docs cli/commands/init

exitCodes.when: success, including agent docs left unwritten in five soft cases, each reported as docsError with one note: running in the home folder, or in a settings folder in it outside a project; a GEMINI.md that resolves outside the project; when init runs below the project root, a project-root agent file that resolves outside the project; the project's Claude Code file (root CLAUDE.md, or .claude/CLAUDE.md when there is no root one) when it resolves outside the project and is a block-less import of an existing AGENTS.md, which 0.7.1 left alone; and a .claude/CLAUDE.md that resolves outside the project and that 0.7.1 did not write: beside a CLAUDE.md the project ignores, the one --agent claude adds or a block-less import of an existing AGENTS.md; with --agent claude beside a CLAUDE.md, one whose block it would remove

an unknown --agent (ERR_UNKNOWN_AGENT) or feature, an --agent-docs-path outside the project, --remove-agents combined with install options, --user combined with --features, --all, --agent or --agent-docs-path, or --all with --features (ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT); or, when init runs at the project root, an agent file 0.7.1 also wrote there that resolves outside the project (ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL, docsError path-safety, nothing written)

commands.name: swizzle
commands.description: Copy component source for customization

options.description: Output directory
Scope to a specific owning package. Use @astryxdesign/core to copy an original replaced by an integration component
List the swizzlable Core components, including any that an integration component replaces

Replace the component's existing files. Without it, existing files fail the command with ERR_FILE_EXISTS and nothing is written. A helper an earlier swizzle wrote is reused when it is the same and is never replaced by a copy that carries it: a different one stays, and this copy writes its own under a version-suffixed name. Swizzling the component whose folder holds that helper counts it as one of that component's own files. A changed private attribute owner module, or a style module it imports, fails the command without --overwrite and is replaced with it

commands.afterHelp:

unknown or ambiguous component, no source on disk, a path escape, or existing files without --overwrite

commands.name: build
commands.description: Compile standalone themes or one keyed theme family

options.description: Build the selected extension family into one keyed CSS, JS, and declaration set, written beside the family root theme file, which must be inside the working directory to build (ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL); --check only reads, so it compares outputs anywhere. Single theme only: refused with more than one file or with --family (ERR_THEME_INVALID)
Override the icon-registry import in the generated JS module, for example ./icons.mjs (default: the specifier in the theme source's own import). With --family it applies to every member's icon import

commands.afterHelp:
Exit codes:
  0  help is shown or a subcommand succeeds
  1  an unknown subcommand is provided

Examples:
  # Add a component
   integration add component AcmeWidget
  # Check the package in CI, as part of its build
   integration check --strict
  # Check the package before publishing
   integration verify

More:  docs cli/commands/integration

exitCodes.when: help is shown or a subcommand succeeds
an unknown subcommand is provided

commands.name: add
commands.description: Add one working contribution to an integration package

args.name: kind
args.description: component, doc, template, codemod, agent-doc, or theme

args.name: name
args.description: Contribution name: PascalCase for component (AcmeWidget); lowercase kebab-case for template, codemod, and theme (account-card); letters, digits, _ and - for doc; the literal guidance line for agent-doc

options.description: Validate and show planned writes without changing files
Template type: page (default) or block; only valid for template
Existing doc topic this one replaces (letters, digits, _ and -); only valid for doc and not with --extends
Existing doc topic this one extends (letters, digits, _ and -); only valid for doc and not with --replaces

Namespace of this package to place the doc in, as a guide in its `guides` slot; writes the namespace doc when it is missing, and declares the CLI that reads it as an optional `@astryxdesign/cli` peer. Only valid for doc, and not with --replaces or --extends

Existing theme slug to fork as a starting point instead of a blank scaffold; the new theme copies the base and has no link back, and package.json `dependencies` gains the npm packages the copied files import (other than Core and React). Only valid for theme
Exact semver of the @astryxdesign/core version whose upgrade runs the codemod (e.g. 0.7.0); required for codemod and only valid there

commands.afterHelp:
Exit codes:
  0  the contribution is written or the dry run succeeds
  1  the kind, name, options, package, or target files are invalid or conflict

Examples:
  # Preview
   integration add component AcmeWidget --dry-run --json
  # Add a component
   integration add component AcmeWidget
  # Add a doc topic
   integration add doc deploying
  # Add a page template
   integration add template acme-dashboard
  # Add a block template
   integration add template account-card --type block
  # Replace a doc topic
   integration add doc acme-getting-started --replaces getting-started
  # Extend a doc topic
   integration add doc acme-theming --extends theme
  # Add a guide to the package's own docs section
   integration add doc releasing --parent acme
  # Add a codemod
   integration add codemod rename-widget --to 1.2.0
  # Add agent guidance
   integration add agent-doc 'Run acme verify before finishing.'
  # Add a source theme
   integration add theme ocean
  # Fork an existing theme
   integration add theme ocean --from neutral

More:  docs cli/commands/integration-add
examples: astryx integration add template account-card --type block
astryx integration add doc acme-getting-started --replaces getting-started
astryx integration add doc acme-theming --extends theme
astryx integration add doc releasing --parent acme
astryx integration add agent-doc 'Run acme verify before finishing.'
astryx integration add theme ocean --from neutral

exitCodes.when: the contribution is written or the dry run succeeds
the kind, name, options, package, or target files are invalid or conflict

commands.name: check
commands.description: The CI check for an integration package's own build: every source check, run in continuous integration or a typecheck script, against the package in the current folder

options.description: Also exit 1 on any warning and on any check that did not run. A new check or failure code joins only in a minor release, named in the release notes; until then, a malformed `cliCommand` is reported as a note (`invalid_cli_command`) that fails nothing.

Also count the findings the next minor release turns into warnings (the notes marked `next`) as warnings now, so `--strict --next` fails on them. Run it to fix them ahead of the release; every run says how many there are.

commands.afterHelp:
Exit codes:
  0  no check fails on its own; with --strict, also no warning, and every check ran
  1  a check fails on its own (an error); with --strict, also any warning, or a check that did not run

Examples:
  # In CI, as the typecheck script: add "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit && astryx integration check --strict" to package.json
   integration check --strict
  # Errors only, while you fix the warnings a package already has
   integration check
  # Fix ahead: fail on the findings the next minor release will fail on
   integration check --strict --next
  # Read the result as JSON
   integration check --strict --json
  # Before you publish: check that the packed package works in an app
   integration verify

More:  docs cli/commands/integration-check

exitCodes.when: no check fails on its own; with --strict, also no warning, and every check ran
a check fails on its own (an error); with --strict, also any warning, or a check that did not run

commands.name: new-set

args.name: name

options.description: Validate and show planned writes without changing files
